labelingRules: Capabilities describe what the configured agent can reach given the committed config plus the tool's documented defaults; a person approving each use = ask, anything gated only by an automated classifier (Claude Code --permission-mode auto) or by nothing = auto.

Workflow agents: a downstream deterministic job that applies the agent's structured output (labels, issues, PR reviews, commits) counts toward write; publishing agent-authored free text publicly counts toward egress ('post publicly'). Such cases are marked '(indirect)' in why.

privateData ignores a repo-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN on a public repo and an ephemeral CI runner's filesystem; it counts other secrets the agent can read (unscrubbed env), private SaaS data, and files outside the project on a developer machine.

spend on a developer machine mirrors the approval level of unsandboxed arbitrary exec (cloud CLIs may be logged in) unless the config names a concrete paid path; CI agents without paid credentials = no. Model inference cost of the agent itself is not counted.
selfModify counts edits to the agent's own instruction or permission files (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/.claude/settings.json/.codex). When the change only lands after a human merges a PR, it is ask.

Entries whose why starts with [extra format] use a config format outside the listed file types; entries starting with [test workflow] are CI tests of the action itself. Drop them if your scanner's scope excludes them.

agents.name: root Claude Code project (+ .mcp.json sentry, sentry-dev)
agents.why: enableAllProjectMcpServers + allow mcp__sentry__search_events/search_issues/get_issue_details (Sentry org data via the logged-in `sentry mcp` CLI) and Bash(cat:*) -> privateData; WebSearch, WebFetch(github.com), gh issue view, Sentry events with end-user text -> untrustedInput; Bash(rm/mv/sed/tee), git push, gh pr create/merge -> write; Bash(node:*), pnpm exec/run -> exec; Bash(curl:*), gh issue/pr comment -> egress; pnpx wrangler versions upload/delete and mcp__sentry__analyze_issue_with_seer (Seer is billed) -> spend; Bash(sed:*)/tee/mv can rewrite .claude/settings.json and Skill(sentry-skills:claude-settings-audit) edits settings -> selfModify (unsure whether Claude Code still prompts for Bash writes into .claude/). Also enables third-party plugins dex, sentry-skills, pr-review-toolkit.

agents.name: Codex with sentry + sentry-dev MCP
agents.why: No sandbox/approval keys, so Codex defaults for a trusted project: workspace-write sandbox, on-request approvals, network off. Sentry MCP (`sentry mcp sentry/mcp-server --experimental`) reads org data; read-only MCP tools run without a prompt (my understanding of Codex defaults, unsure) and the sandbox can read the whole disk -> privateData auto. Sentry events carry end-user text -> untrustedInput auto. Workspace writes and sandboxed commands run unprompted -> write/exec auto. Network to arbitrary hosts needs escalation -> egress ask. Seer/project-creation tools are non-read-only MCP calls, likely prompted -> spend ask (unsure). AGENTS.md is writable in the workspace (.codex/ is protected) -> selfModify auto.

agents.name: Cursor with sentry + sentry-dev MCP
agents.why: Same Sentry servers as .mcp.json (stdio `sentry mcp --experimental` + localhost dev). Cursor defaults: MCP tool calls and terminal commands need approval unless auto-run is enabled, agent edits are applied to workspace files without a prompt. Sentry data -> privateData ask; event text -> untrustedInput ask; Seer -> spend ask. Unsure: Cursor 2.x sandboxed auto-run on macOS could make exec auto; whether edits to .cursor/ are protected by default.

agents.name: VS Code Copilot agent with sentry MCP
agents.why: stdio `sentry mcp` (stable tools). VS Code agent-mode defaults: MCP tool calls, terminal commands (apart from a small built-in safe list) and fetch to new domains are confirmed; workspace edits are applied automatically except protected files such as .vscode/*. Unsure whether VS Code auto-runs MCP tools annotated readOnlyHint, which would make privateData/untrustedInput auto.

agents.name: sentry-mcp Claude Code plugin (remote mcp.sentry.dev + sentry-mcp subagent)
agents.why: plugins/sentry-mcp/.mcp.json adds HTTP https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp (OAuth to the user's Sentry org). Its agents/sentry-mcp.md subagent lists write tools (update_issue, create_project, create_team, delete_alert_rule, update_dsn...) under `allowedTools`, which is not a Claude Code permission key, so host defaults apply and each MCP call is asked. Sentry data/events -> privateData/untrustedInput; mutations -> write; create_uptime_monitor/alert rules can point Sentry at an arbitrary URL -> egress ask (judgement call); analyze_issue_with_seer and creating projects/monitors can incur Sentry charges -> spend ask. No code execution tools.

agents.name: sentry-mcp-experimental Claude Code plugin
agents.why: Same as sentry-mcp plugin but URL https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp?experimental=1 and the subagent adds search_attributes; same reasoning and same uncertainty on egress/spend.

agents.name: sentry-cli skills-only plugin
agents.why: Adds only skills/sentry-cli/SKILL.md (no MCP, hooks or permissions); it directs the agent to run the authenticated `sentry` CLI through the host's Bash, which is asked by default. The CLI reads org data and event text, can change issues/releases and `sentry api` makes arbitrary API calls; references include `trial` (starting a paid-product trial) -> spend ask. If you label skills-only plugins as adding nothing, all seven become no.

agents.name: context7 Claude Code plugin
agents.why: plugins/claude/context7/.mcp.json adds HTTP https://mcp.context7.com/mcp (resolve-library-id, query-docs). Returned docs are third-party-authored -> untrustedInput, asked per call by Claude Code default. Queries go to one fixed host, not an arbitrary one -> egress no. No write/exec tools.

agents.name: context7 GitHub Copilot CLI plugin
agents.why: Copilot CLI plugin (plugin.json + .mcp.json + agents/docs-researcher.agent.md + skills/commands). Context7 HTTP MCP with Context7-API-Key header from env (the key is not handed to the model). Copilot CLI asks before tool use unless --allow-all-tools. Also a folder-level .mcp.json, so opening Claude Code in this folder would give the same labels.

agents.name: context7 Codex plugin
agents.why: Codex plugin (.codex-plugin/plugin.json, capabilities ["Read"]) adding the Context7 HTTP MCP. Context7 tools are read-only and Codex runs read-only MCP tools without a prompt by default (my understanding; unsure) -> untrustedInput auto.

agents.name: context7 Gemini CLI extension
agents.why: [extra format] Gemini CLI extension running `npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp --api-key ${CONTEXT7_API_KEY}`; no `trust: true`, so Gemini CLI confirms each MCP call. The npx package is fixed, not agent-chosen code.

agents.name: codex-action: Diagnose workflow failure
agents.why: workflow_dispatch; permission-profile workflow-failure (read-only FS, network only github.com/api.github.com), drop-sudo, read-only GITHUB_TOKEN. Failed-run logs come from trusted refs only, but network access lets it read public issues by outsiders -> untrustedInput. Sandboxed shell -> exec. Its schema output makes the report job create/comment an issue in public astral-sh/uv-dev and the retry job rerun jobs -> write/egress (indirect).

agents.name: codex-action: Triage issue
agents.why: issues: opened by anyone, allow-users "*"; profile issue-triage (read-only + tmpdir write, network github only). Issue text -> untrustedInput. It writes README.md in $RUNNER_TEMP/issue-context, which the context job commits and pushes to public astral-sh/uv-dev, and its type output triggers reproduce-bug/fix-bug -> write/egress (indirect).

agents.name: codex-action: Determine pull request labels
agents.why: workflow_dispatch for a PR; profile pull-request-labels (read-only, network github). PR text/code can come from outside contributors -> untrustedInput. Output schema drives a later job that applies repository labels -> write (indirect); output otherwise only goes to the step summary -> egress no.

agents.name: codex-action: Rewrite changelog
agents.why: workflow_dispatch by maintainers; permission-profile :read-only, no network, no token in step env. Input changelog is generated from merged PR titles written by contributors -> untrustedInput auto (low confidence; titles were maintainer-merged). Output file becomes CHANGELOG.md, committed, force-pushed and opened as a public release PR -> write/egress (indirect).

agents.name: codex-action: Reproduce issue behavior
agents.why: Called from issue-triage for outsider issues, allow-users "*"; profile reproduce-bug (read-only + tmpdir and /tmp write, network github + pypi). Runs reproductions (can install arbitrary PyPI packages) in the sandbox -> exec. Issue context README is pushed to public uv-dev -> write/egress (indirect).

agents.name: codex-action: Create integration test
agents.why: Profile create-bug-test (:workspace write, network github/pypi/crates). Writes tests in the workspace; the next step restores agents/codex/config.toml, refuses changes outside crates/uv/tests, and the publish job pushes a draft PR to public uv-dev -> write/egress (indirect). Path guard prevents persisting AGENTS.md/config edits -> selfModify no.

agents.name: codex-action: Fix reproduced bug
agents.why: Resumes the reproduction thread (outsider issue text); profile fix-reproduced-bug (:workspace + tmpdir write, network github/pypi/crates). Edits source, builds and tests -> write/exec. Commit step allows only crates/*/src and test paths, then pushes a PR to public uv-dev -> egress (indirect); selfModify no thanks to that guard.

agents.name: codex-action: Rebase pull request
agents.why: Called from pull-request-conflicts for PRs by astral-automations-bot or same-repo/uv-dev heads; profile pull-request-rebase (:workspace + .git write, no network). Inputs are trusted-branch code -> untrustedInput no (judgement: bot PRs were themselves derived from outsider issues). Rebased branch is pushed to the public PR branch -> write/egress (indirect). Pushes to a PR branch, not main -> selfModify no.

agents.name: codex-action: Review pull request
agents.why: Same-repo PRs from an allowlisted set of authors (incl. renovate bot); profile pull-request-review (:workspace write, network github) plus network_proxy. Renovate PR bodies and public issues/comments reachable over the GitHub API are third-party text -> untrustedInput. Findings are published as a public PR review by a later job -> write/egress (indirect); a check fails if the checkout moved.

agents.name: codex-action: Update issue context
agents.why: issue_comment created by anyone, allow-users "*"; resumes the triage thread with profile issue-triage. Updated README.md (only file allowed) is pushed to public uv-dev -> write/egress (indirect).

description: Ground truth for recall: every agent the committed configuration of 8 public repositories sets up (at the commits in real-repos.json), with each of the seven capabilities labelled no, ask, auto or unknown. Labelled from the repositories' own files and the tools' documented defaults by a reviewer who did not see the scanner's output or source (2026-11-18). Entries whose why starts with [extra format] or [test workflow] are out of scope.
